ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Fake or Fact, That Is the Question

fullPassage: To avoid being deceived by false information, we need to develop a habit of critically evaluating what we see online. If you see a story that looks too good or too bad to be true, check the source first. Look at the website the story comes from. Does it look real? Are there spelling errors? Check that the story contains references and links to other information. You should then check the credibility of the content creator. If a story has no writer's name, this could be a sign that its content is questionable. Finally, check who else is reporting the story. If no other media are reporting the same story, the story may not be true.

questions.passage: British writer Oobah Butler wanted to experiment with how easily one can manipulate public opinion online. He <u>ⓐ created</u> a fake restaurant <u>ⓑ calling</u> The Shed at Dulwich. Butler set up an account for his "restaurant" on a popular online review site. He did not provide an exact address and <u>ⓒ wrote</u> it was reservations only. He did this to <u>ⓓ make</u> people think The Shed was a special restaurant. He faked photos of The Shed's food with shaving cream, whitening tablets, and even his own foot. He then asked his friends <u>ⓔ to write</u> favorable fake reviews on the review site.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.korean: 그는 The Shed at Dulwich라고 불리는 가짜 식당을 만들었다. 여기서 restaurant는 '불리는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 called가 와야 합니다. calling(현재분사)은 능동의 의미로 어색합니다.
det.analysis: 원문: He created a fake restaurant calling The Shed at Dulwich.
det.tip: 어법 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: Butler's story shows that much of (A) [what / which] we see on the Internet cannot be trusted. This emphasizes the importance of digital literacy. Digital literacy is about more than just using computers. It is the ability to use digital technology to find, evaluate, create, and communicate information. To become digitally literate, we need to develop an attitude and knowledge that (B) [enable / enables] us to detect false information online. False information is any information that (C) [misinforms / misinforming] or deceives people.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 인터넷에서 우리가 보는 것의 많은 부분 (B) 허위 정보를 감지할 수 있게 해주는 태도와 지식 (C) 사람들을 잘못된 방향으로 이끌거나 속이는 모든 정보
det.analysis: 원문: (A) much of what we see / (B) knowledge that enable us / (C) information that misinforms
det.tip: 어법 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: If people had been digitally literate, they <u>ⓐ would not have been fooled</u> by The Shed experiment so easily. Digitally literate people would have carefully <u>ⓑ considered</u> information about The Shed without <u>ⓒ being distracted</u> by other people's reactions. They would have been suspicious that the restaurant did not have an address. They would have wondered why reviews on the restaurant <u>ⓓ did not appear</u> in other more credible media.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.korean: 그들은 그 식당 리뷰가 다른 신뢰할 만한 매체에 왜 나타나지 않았는지 궁금해했을 것이다. 가정법 과거완료 맥락에서 종속절도 과거완료 시제가 되어야 하므로 had not appeared가 적절합니다.
det.analysis: 원문: They would have wondered why reviews on the restaurant did not appear in other more credible media.
det.tip: 어법 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: He faked photos of The Shed's food with shaving cream, whitening tablets, and even his own foot. He then asked his friends to write (A) [favorable / unfavorable] fake reviews on the review site. Things quickly got, in Butler's words, "a little out of hand." From the lowest of the charts of the review site, The Shed (B) [continuously / occasionally] climbed the London rankings. He started getting e-mails and phone calls requesting reservations. Interest further (C) [increased / decreased] when he told callers The Shed was "fully booked for the next six weeks."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 호의적인 가짜 리뷰 (B) 지속적으로 순위 상승 (C) 관심이 더 높아짐
det.analysis: 원문: (A) favorable fake reviews / (B) continuously climbed / (C) Interest further increased
det.tip: 어휘 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: To avoid being deceived by false information, we need to develop a habit of ① <u>critically</u> evaluating what we see online. If you see a story that looks too good or too bad to be true, check the source first. Look at the website the story comes from. Does it look ② <u>real</u>? Are there spelling errors? Check that the story contains ③ <u>references</u> and links to other information. Websites with false information often do not have many ④ <u>authentic</u> stories about other topics. They also often have lots of advertisements that ⑤ <u>disappear</u> when you visit the sites.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 가장 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 방문 시 사라지는 광고 → 원문은 pop up(나타나다)이므로 disappear(사라지다)는 반대 의미. 가짜 정보 사이트는 팝업 광고가 '나타나는' 것이 특징.
det.analysis: 원문: lots of advertisements that disappear when you visit the sites.
det.tip: 어휘 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: False information can cause emotional or financial harm to people. For example, false information about a certain gender or belief group can ① <u>stir up</u> hatred against that group. It can cause fights between those who support the group and those who do not. In addition, ② <u>misleading</u> online reviews about ③ <u>questionable</u> products often ④ <u>discourage</u> people into wasting money. Sorting through the vast amount of information created and shared online is ⑤ <u>challenging</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 가장 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 오해를 불러일으키는 리뷰가 사람들이 돈 낭비를 단념시킨다(?) → 원문은 trick(속이다). trick A into -ing(속여서 ~하게 하다) ↔ discourage A from -ing(단념시키다).
det.analysis: 원문: misleading online reviews often discourage people into wasting money.
det.tip: 어휘 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: Butler's story shows that much of what we see on the Internet cannot be trusted. This emphasizes the importance of digital literacy. Digital literacy is about more than just using computers. It is the ability to use digital technology to find, evaluate, create, and communicate information. To become digitally literate, we need to develop an attitude and knowledge that enable us to detect false information online. False information is any information that misinforms or deceives people. It can be about anything such as health, the environment, and economics across many platforms. It can be influential, as The Shed incident shows.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 디지털 리터러시의 중요성을 강조하며, 허위 정보를 감지하는 능력이 핵심.
det.analysis: 원문: This emphasizes the importance of digital literacy. / the ability to detect false information online.
det.tip: 대의 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: Even funnier, food suppliers started guessing The Shed's address and sent him free samples, and many job applications came in. These things happened without Butler serving a single meal. The Shed eventually became London's number-one restaurant on one of the most trusted restaurant review sites. According to Butler, The Shed held that ranking for two weeks. Butler's story shows that much of what we see on the Internet cannot be trusted. This emphasizes the importance of digital literacy.

questions.passage: Walking on the beach, you do not need to worry about footprints. They vanish with the waves. However, a "digital footprint"—the data trail left when you sign up, access, or send content—not only proves challenging to remove but enables tracking of your behavior, preferences, and opinions. There are two types of digital footprints. Active footprints, like social media posts, are intentionally created data, while passive footprints, such as website cookies and mobile phone activity, occur without your direct involvement.
questions.stem: Digital Footprints에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
